CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bangka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interaction normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to perform household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers by their own will and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.

STRATEGY FOR WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION Article 24 (1) Women's empowerment and protection shall be implemented by integrating gender mainstreaming and gender-disaggregated data in an integrated manner based on applicable laws and regulations.
(2) In women's empowerment and protection, a Working Group and Integrated Services shall be established as determined by Regent's Decree. (3) Women's empowerment and protection shall be coordinated by the Agency responsible for Women's Empowerment.

a. conducting monitoring and evaluation periodically on the implementation of programs and activities that have been implemented; and b. preparing reports periodically.

Article 21
(1) The implementation of Protection for women victims of disaster as referred to in Article 13 letter h is in the context of providing protection during disaster and post-disaster.
(2) Women victims of disaster as referred to in paragraph (1) receive protection for:
a. access to proper housing;
b. health services;
c. information access services and legal consultation; and
d. post-disaster recovery.

CHAPTER IX
FINANCING
Article 27
All costs for the implementation of planning policies, programs and activities related to Women's Empowerment and Protection are sourced from: a. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
c. Other legitimate and non-binding sources in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 22
(1) The implementation of Protection for female commercial sex workers as referred to in Article 13 letter i is in the context of providing health protection and improving life skills capabilities as capital to enhance social status.
(2) Protection for female commercial sex workers as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. providing life skills capabilities;
b. facilitating reproductive health services; and
c. preventing the occurrence of human trafficking.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of Government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bangka Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bangka Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
17. Elderly Women are persons who have reached 60 years of age and above.
18. Women with Disabilities are women who experience physical and/or mental barriers that interfere with their activities and social interaction normally.
19. Homeless Women are women who do not have a permanent place of residence and for various reasons must live under bridges, public parks, roadsides or various other public facilities to sleep and carry out daily life.
20. Domestic Women Workers are people who work for a person or several people in a household to perform household work for wages.
21. Women Heads of Households are women who for various reasons are left by their husbands, and ultimately act or contribute and function to carry out the role and responsibilities as head of household.
22. Women Former Inmates of Correctional Institutions are women who have served sentences in correctional institutions.
23. Women Disaster Victims are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
24. Women Commercial Sex Workers are women who work as sex workers by their own will and/or are prostituted.
25. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience physical, mental suffering and/or economic loss resulting from a criminal act.

The relevant sentence was in the retrieved candidates, so the error is the judge’s over-interpretation.

Article 8

a. provision of skills and job training;
b. facilitation of the formation of productive economic business groups; c. facilitation of strengthening and development of productive economic business groups; d. facilitation and capital assistance; and
e. facilitation of marketing network development.

Article 26

(3) The formulation of policy for program and activity planning for the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is coordinated by the Regional Apparatus in charge of Regency development planning.
(4) The budgeting of programs and activities as referred to in Article 25 letter b is implemented through general budget policy as set forth in the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.
(5) The implementation of programs and activities as referred to in Article 25 letter c is implemented through:
a. implementation of programs and activities as set forth in the budget document of the Regional Apparatus; and
b. coordination and synchronization of the implementation of programs and activities with related Regional Apparatus.

CHAPTER VIII
MECHANISM FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND
PROTECTION
Article 25
The mechanism for the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is carried out through the following stages:
a. formulation of policy, program planning and activities; b. budgeting of programs and activities;
c. implementation of programs and activities; and
d. monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

Article 9
Empowerment of women in the social and cultural field as referred to in Article 7 letter b shall be implemented through:
a. enhancement of knowledge, attitudes and skills to encourage the fulfillment of tiered education in accordance with potential to improve social status;
b. enhancement of awareness, willingness and ability to overcome; c. health problems through quality promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts primarily in the field of reproductive health; d. enhancement of awareness and knowledge about family planning; e. independence, health and welfare including access to consultation services and marriage registration; and
f. facilitation and efforts to preserve customs and traditions and development of science, technology, arts and culture for the advancement of women.

CHAPTER VII
STRATEGY FOR WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION Article 24 (1) Women's empowerment and protection shall be implemented by integrating gender mainstreaming and gender-disaggregated data in an integrated manner based on applicable laws and regulations.
(2) In women's empowerment and protection, a Working Group and Integrated Services shall be established as determined by Regent's Decree. (3) Women's empowerment and protection shall be coordinated by the Agency responsible for Women's Empowerment.

Article 23
(1) The Implementation of Protection for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 13 letter j is in the context of providing legal protection and/or recovery from trauma and health.
(2) Protection for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. legal assistance;
b. assistance following the occurrence of acts of violence;
c. rehabilitation and social reintegration; and
d. trauma and health services.

7.3.rationale: The golden label is “No,” but the Indonesian text explicitly mentions “bantuan internasional” (international assistance) in Pasal 28(2) huruf g: “mengoordinasikan peran serta dunia usaha dan kelembagaan lain, termasuk bantuan internasional bagi pemberdayaan dan perlindungan perempuan.” That is direct evidence of international assistance/donor involvement (at least as a contemplated support source/partner). The judge’s “Yes” is therefore supported by the document; the discrepancy arises because the golden label appears inconsistent with the text.
